message.text: The auth interceptor lives at web/src/connect.ts. It manages access tokens and refresh logic. The backend validation package is server/auth. I am reading the relevant files to confirm the exact details.

The frontend auth interceptor lives in `web/src/connect.ts`. It manages access tokens (Bearer) stored in localStorage via `auth-state.ts`.

Refresh tokens are sent as cookies via fetchWithCredentials. Backend validation is handled by the `server/auth` package, specifically its `Authenticator` and `NewAuthInterceptor`.

The frontend interceptor attaches a Bearer access token to API requests. Token refresh uses a cookie via the RefreshToken RPC.

The backend validates JWT V2 access tokens and refresh tokens. The frontend interceptor does not manage PATs.

q29.
web/src/connect.ts; access token (Bearer) and refresh token (cookie); server/auth

`authInterceptor` in `web/src/connect.ts` sets `Authorization: Bearer` from `web/src/auth-state.ts` and refreshes via `AuthService.refreshToken` with `credentials: "include"`. The backend validates those in `server/auth` (`Authenticator`: access-token JWT, refresh-token cookie, and PAT for non-browser clients). Connect/gateway attach that via `NewAuthInterceptor` / gateway middleware in `server/router/api/v1/v1.go`.
